 Coach Kenny Dillingham said his teams have flown out on Fridays whenever they’ve played a game two time zones away. “You can’t predict a worldwide stoppage,” he said. Christian Petersen / Getty Images 
 By Bruce Feldman Nov. 13, 2026 Updated Nov. 14, 2026 7:13 pm EST Share article 65 The Athletic has live coverage of Texas vs. LSU. 
 Coaches constantly preach about overcoming adversity, but they are often most concerned with how their teams adjust and adapt. Most coaches double down on such things during games or in practice. But for some teams this weekend, such as Arizona State, those lessons will be as much about what happens before the game.
 Advertisement
 Arizona State is scheduled to play at UCF on Saturday, with the kickoff time originally set for 3:30 p.m. ET. But the Sun Devils — along with many other programs and millions of Americans — had their travel plans halted when the Federal Aviation Administration grounded all domestic departures at 3:54 p.m. ET Friday.
 For two hours, the Arizona State team sat on a plane awaiting takeoff to Orlando, Fla. Eventually, the Sun Devils made their way out of a packed airport to return to the team’s facility. Normally, big-time football programs schedule their travel itinerary down to the minute, but suddenly everything was up in the air — just not the team plane.
 “All of our luggage is still on the plane,” ASU strength coach Joe Connolly said. “Lots of guys are without their wallets and keys.”
 Some 20 to 30 Sun Devil players are expected to be without access to their apartments Friday night, Connolly told The Athletic .
 “It’s been kind of a nightmare, but you just gotta roll with the punches,” he said. “This is more of a mindset type of thing rather than a physiological type of deal.”
 ASU’s tentative plan is to have a team meeting at 5 a.m. local time, fly out at 6 a.m., land by noon ET and head to the team hotel for a pregame meal and a little clap session.
 “We really don’t have time to do anything else,” Connolly said. “We barely have enough time to get our pregame meal down the hatch.”
 The FAA lifted the nationwide ground stop a little after 10 p.m. ET Friday. The schools soon announced that the game will now kick off at 5:30 pm ET.
 Even with the delayed start, trying to get the players loose and primed after they have sat four-plus hours during a roughly 1,900-mile flight to play a game a few hours after landing presents unique challenges. Team training staff can help with soft tissue work and resistance bands to get the players warmed up.
 Advertisement
 Coach Kenny Dillingham said his teams have flown out on Fridays whenever they’ve played a game two time zones away. “You can’t predict a worldwide stoppage,” he said.
 The 36-year-old said his team will be mentally ready. “I’ve coached high school games before where we’ve had four-hour bus rides, so let’s dance!
 “There’s really nothing you can do about it. It is what it is. And it’s not like they’re gonna count it as 0.75 in the loss column if you lose. If you make a big deal about it with your team, then it’s a big deal. I’m trying to make it as un-big-of-a-deal as we can.”
